A1.name: Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) Skills and the Mathematical Processes
A1.description: apply, to the best of their ability, a variety of social-emotional learning skills to support their use of the mathematical processes and their learning in connection with the expectations in the other five strands of the mathematics curriculum

A1.1.description: Identify and manage emotions, so they can express and manage their feelings, and show understanding of the feelings of others, as they engage positively in mathematics activities

A1.2.description: Recognize sources of stress and cope with challenges, so they can work through challenging math problems, understanding that their resourcefulness in using various strategies to respond to stress is helping them build personal resilience

A1.3.description: Maintain positive motivation and perseverance, so they can recognize that testing out different approaches to problems and learning from mistakes is an important part of the learning process, and is aided by a sense of optimism and hope

A1.4.description: Build relationships and communicate effectively, so they can work collaboratively on math problems – expressing their thinking, listening to the thinking of others, and practising inclusivity – and in that way foster healthy relationships

A1.5.description: Develop self-awareness and sense of identity, so they can see themselves as capable math learners, and strengthen their sense of ownership of their learning, as part of their emerging sense of identity and belonging

A1.6.description: Think critically and creatively, so they can make connections between math and everyday contexts to help them make informed judgements and decisions

B1.name: Number Sense
B1.description: demonstrate an understanding of numbers and make connections to the way numbers are used in everyday life

B1.1.description: Read and represent whole numbers up to and including 50, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life

B1.2.description: Compose and decompose whole numbers up to and including 50, using a variety of tools and strategies, in various contexts

B1.3.description: Compare and order whole numbers up to and including 50, in various contexts

B1.4.description: Estimate the number of objects in collections of up to 50, and verify their estimates by counting

B1.5.description: Count to 50 by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s, using a variety of tools and strategies

B1.6.description: Use drawings to represent and solve fair-share problems that involve 2 and 4 sharers, respectively, and have remainders of 1 or 2

B1.7.description: Recognize that one half and two fourths of the same whole are equal, in fair-sharing contexts

B1.8.description: Use drawings to compare and order unit fractions representing the individual portions that result when a whole is shared by different numbers of sharers, up to a maximum of 10

B2.name: Operations
B2.description: use knowledge of numbers and operations to solve mathematical problems encountered in everyday life

B2.1.description: Use the properties of addition and subtraction, and the relationship between addition and subtraction, to solve problems and check calculations

B2.2.description: Recall and demonstrate addition facts for numbers up to 10, and related subtraction facts

B2.3.description: Use mental math strategies, including estimation, to add and subtract whole numbers that add up to no more than 20, and explain the strategies used

B2.4.description: Use objects, diagrams, and equations to represent, describe, and solve situations involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 50

B2.5.description: Represent and solve equal-group problems where the total number of items is no more than 10, including problems in which each group is a half, using tools and drawings

C1.name: Patterns and Relationships
C1.description: identify, describe, extend, create, and make predictions about a variety of patterns, including those found in real-life contexts

C1.1.description: Identify and describe the regularities in a variety of patterns, including patterns found in real-life contexts

C1.2.description: Create and translate patterns using movements, sounds, objects, shapes, letters, and numbers

C1.3.description: Determine pattern rules and use them to extend patterns, make and justify predictions, and identify missing elements in patterns

C1.4.description: Create and describe patterns to illustrate relationships among whole numbers up to 50

C2.name: Equations and Inequalities
C2.description: demonstrate an understanding of variables, expressions, equalities, and inequalities, and apply this understanding in various contexts

C2.1.description: Identify quantities that can change and quantities that always remain the same in real-life contexts

C2.2.description: Determine whether given pairs of addition and subtraction expressions are equivalent or not

C2.3.description: Identify and use equivalent relationships for whole numbers up to 50, in various contexts

C3.name: Coding
C3.description: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations using coding concepts and skills

C3.1.description: Solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential events

C3.2.description: Read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes

D1.name: Data Literacy
D1.description: manage, analyse, and use data to make convincing arguments and informed decisions, in various contexts drawn from real life

D1.1.description: Sort sets of data about people or things according to one attribute, and describe rules used for sorting

D1.2.description: Collect data through observations, experiments, and interviews to answer questions of interest that focus on a single piece of information; record the data using methods of their choice; and organize the data in tally tables

D1.3.description: Display sets of data, using one-to-one correspondence, in concrete graphs and pictographs with proper sources, titles, and labels

D1.4.description: Order categories of data from greatest to least frequency for various data sets displayed in tally tables, concrete graphs, and pictographs

D1.5.description: Analyse different sets of data presented in various ways, including in tally tables, concrete graphs, and pictographs, by asking and answering questions about the data and drawing conclusions, then make convincing arguments and informed decisions

D2.name: Probability
D2.description: describe the likelihood that events will happen, and use that information to make predictions

D2.1.description: Use mathematical language, including the terms “impossible”, “possible”, and “certain”, to describe the likelihood of events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions

D2.2.description: Make and test predictions about the likelihood that the categories in a data set from one population will have the same frequencies in data collected from a different population of the same size

E1.description: describe and represent shape, location, and movement by applying geometric properties and spatial relationships in order to navigate the world around them

E1.1.description: Sort three-dimensional objects and two-dimensional shapes according to one attribute at a time, and identify the sorting rule being used

A1.4.description: Build relationships and communicate effectively, so they can work collaboratively on math problems – expressing their thinking, listening to the thinking of others, and practising inclusivity – and in that way foster healthy relationships

A1.5.description: Develop self-awareness and sense of identity, so they can see themselves as capable math learners, and strengthen their sense of ownership of their learning, as part of their emerging sense of identity and belonging

A1.6.description: Think critically and creatively, so they can make connections between math and everyday contexts to help them make informed judgements and decisions

B1.name: Number Sense
B1.description: demonstrate an understanding of numbers and make connections to the way numbers are used in everyday life

B1.1.description: Represent and compare very large and very small numbers, including through the use of scientific notation, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life

B1.2.description: Describe, compare, and order numbers in the real number system (rational and irrational numbers), separately and in combination, in various contexts

B1.3.description: Estimate and calculate square roots, in various contexts

B1.4.description: Use fractions, decimal numbers, and percents, including percents of more than 100% or less than 1%, interchangeably and flexibly to solve a variety of problems

B2.name: Operations
B2.description: use knowledge of numbers and operations to solve mathematical problems encountered in everyday life

B2.1.description: Use the properties and order of operations, and the relationships between operations, to solve problems involving rational numbers, ratios, rates, and percents, including those requiring multiple steps or multiple operations

B2.2.description: Understand and recall commonly used square numbers and their square roots

B2.3.description: Use mental math strategies to multiply and divide whole numbers and decimal numbers up to thousandths by powers of ten, and explain the strategies used

B2.4.description: Add and subtract integers, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts

B2.5.description: Add and subtract fractions, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts

B2.6.description: Multiply and divide fractions by fractions, as well as by whole numbers and mixed numbers, in various contexts

B2.7.description: Multiply and divide integers, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts

B2.8.description: Compare proportional situations and determine unknown values in proportional situations, and apply proportional reasoning to solve problems in various contexts

C1.name: Patterns and Relationships
C1.description: identify, describe, extend, create, and make predictions about a variety of patterns, including those found in real-life contexts

C1.1.description: Identify and compare a variety of repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns, including patterns found in real-life contexts, and compare linear growing and shrinking patterns on the basis of their constant rates and initial values

C1.2.description: Create and translate repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns involving rational numbers using various representations, including algebraic expressions and equations for linear growing and shrinking patterns

C1.3.description: Determine pattern rules and use them to extend patterns, make and justify predictions, and identify missing elements in growing and shrinking patterns involving rational numbers, and use algebraic representations of the pattern rules to solve for unknown values in linear growing and shrinking patterns

C1.4.description: Create and describe patterns to illustrate relationships among rational numbers

C2.name: Equations and Inequalities
C2.description: demonstrate an understanding of variables, expressions, equations, and inequalities, and apply this understanding in various contexts

C2.1.description: Add and subtract monomials with a degree of 1, and add binomials with a degree of 1 that involve integers, using tools

C2.2.description: Evaluate algebraic expressions that involve rational numbers

C2.3.description: Solve equations that involve multiple terms, integers, and decimal numbers in various contexts, and verify solutions

C2.4.description: Solve inequalities that involve integers, and verify and graph the solutions

C3.name: Coding
C3.description: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations using coding concepts and skills

C3.1.description: Solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves the analysis of data in order to inform and communicate decisions

C3.2.description: Read and alter existing code involving the analysis of data in order to inform and communicate decisions, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes and the efficiency of the code

D1.name: Data Literacy
D1.description: manage, analyse, and use data to make convincing arguments and informed decisions, in various contexts drawn from real life

D1.1.description: Identify situations involving one-variable data and situations involving two-variable data, and explain when each type of data is needed

D1.2.description: Collect continuous data to answer questions of interest involving two variables, and organize the data sets as appropriate in a table of values

D1.3.description: Select from among a variety of graphs, including scatter plots, the type of graph best suited to represent various sets of data; display the data in the graphs with proper sources, titles, and labels, and appropriate scales; and justify their choice of graphs

D1.4.description: Create an infographic about a data set, representing the data in appropriate ways, including in tables and scatter plots, and incorporating any other relevant information that helps to tell a story about the data

D1.5.description: Use mathematical language, including the terms “strong”, “weak”, “none”, “positive”, and “negative”, to describe the relationship between two variables for various data sets with and without outliers

D1.6.description: Analyse different sets of data presented in various ways, including in scatter plots and in misleading graphs, by asking and answering questions about the data, challenging preconceived notions, and drawing conclusions, then make convincing arguments and informed decisions

D2.name: Probability
D2.description: describe the likelihood that events will happen, and use that information to make predictions

D2.1.description: Solve various problems that involve probability, using appropriate tools and strategies, including Venn and tree diagrams

D2.2.description: Determine and compare the theoretical and experimental probabilities of multiple independent events happening and of multiple dependent events happening

E1.name: Geometric and Spatial Reasoning
E1.description: describe and represent shape, location, and movement by applying geometric properties and spatial relationships in order to navigate the world around them

E1.1.description: Identify geometric properties of tessellating shapes and identify the transformations that occur in the tessellations

E1.2.description: Make objects and models using appropriate scales, given their top, front, and side views or their perspective views

E1.3.description: Use scale drawings to calculate actual lengths and areas, and reproduce scale drawings at different ratios

E1.4.description: Describe and perform translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations on a Cartesian plane, and predict the results of these transformations

E2.name: Measurement
E2.description: compare, estimate, and determine measurements in various contexts

E2.1.description: Represent very large (mega, giga, tera) and very small (micro, nano, pico) metric units using models, base ten relationships, and exponential notation

E2.2.description: Solve problems involving angle properties, including the properties of intersecting and parallel lines and of polygons

E2.3.description: Solve problems involving the perimeter, circumference, area, volume, and surface area of composite two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects, using appropriate formulas

E2.4.description: Describe the Pythagorean relationship using various geometric models, and apply the theorem to solve problems involving an unknown side length for a given right triangle

F1.name: Money and Finances
F1.description: demonstrate the knowledge and skills needed to make informed financial decisions

F1.1.description: Describe some advantages and disadvantages of various methods of payment that can be used when dealing with multiple currencies and exchange rates

F1.2.description: Create a financial plan to reach a long-term financial goal, accounting for income, expenses, and tax implications

F1.3.description: Identify different ways to maintain a balanced budget, and use appropriate tools to track all income and spending, for several different scenarios

F1.4.description: Determine the growth of simple and compound interest at various rates using digital tools, and explain the impact interest has on long-term financial planning

F1.5.description: Compare various ways for consumers to get more value for their money when spending, including taking advantage of sales and customer loyalty and incentive programs, and determine the best choice for different scenarios

F1.6.description: Compare interest rates, annual fees, and rewards and other incentives offered by various credit card companies and consumer contracts to determine the best value and the best choice for different scenarios
